title: 他与她的梦 8他与她的梦 7
lines: 楼梯的尽头是空旷的。
格林走完最后一级台阶，站定，环顾四周。这是一个巨大的地下空间，比之前的骸骨大厅更大，穹顶在视线所及之外隐没于黑暗。
地面是某种灰白色的石板，平整整洁，没有任何多余的杂物。空气是安静的，没有风，没有气味，连之前一直若有若无的腐烂气息都消失了。
这里什么都没有。
格林的目光扫过整个空间。空。空得彻底。像是有人把这里的每一粒灰尘都仔细地清除了，只留下这个干净的、没有东西的空地。
“爱丽丝也不在这里。”
格林说，语气似乎依然平静，但是里面的烦躁几乎快要溢出来。大脑越来越不清醒了，再不找到爱丽丝，他都不确定自己会做出什么事情来。
他打算转身离开，然后呼啸声传来。
由远及近的，像是什么东西在高速穿过空气。格林停下动作，抬头。
那只白色的大鸟从穹顶的黑暗中俯冲而下。它的翅膀展开时足有四五米宽，羽毛是那种近乎刺眼的白，在昏暗的光线下反而显得格外清晰。
它的飞行轨迹不像是自然的鸟类——更加笔直、更加具有目的性，像是一支射出的箭。
格林没有躲闪，他站在那里，抬着头，看着那只大鸟越来越近，直到能看得清它的细节：
它的头部很长，比正常的鸟类长得多，像是被拉伸过的。脸上覆盖着细密的白色羽毛，但那些羽毛遮不住底下的轮廓——那线条带着某种不太像鸟类的东西。
它有头发，金色的头发。从头顶垂下来，像是人类的长发，在高速俯冲中被风吹向后方。那些发丝在空气中飘动着，带着一种微弱的、几乎看不见的光泽。
“不是爱丽丝。”格林极其失望地说着。
即使那头发是金色的，但那种金色和爱丽丝的不一样。爱丽丝的金发是明亮的、带着阳光的温度。而这只大鸟的金发是淡的、冷的，像是在月光下洗过很多遍。
大鸟的嘴张开——那嘴像是鸟喙，又像是人的嘴唇，两者之间找不到明确的边界。它发出一声尖锐的啸叫，声音让空气震动。
格林动了，他迎上去，一拳击向大鸟的头部。
大鸟的身体被直接打偏了轨迹。它在空中翻滚了一圈半，羽毛飘落几根，然后扑棱着翅膀重新稳住，落在一段距离之外。
它歪着头看着格林。那双眼睛是琥珀色的，竖瞳——是鸟的眼睛，也是别的什么。
格林看着它，思考着她和爱丽丝可能的关系，虽然她不是爱丽丝，但是没准她和爱丽丝有关系呢？有关系就可能有爱丽丝的线索。
大鸟没有多少反应，它张了张嘴，发出一个模糊的音节——像是想要说什么，但被某种东西堵住了。
然后它再次起飞，这一次它不再正面冲撞。它盘旋着，绕着格林飞了一圈又一圈，翅膀扇动间，空气被切割成一道道无形的利刃。
那些风刃从四面八方向格林袭来，速度极快，角度刁钻，像是活物一样在空中拐弯、追踪。
content_en:
The end of the stairs was empty.
Green walked up the last step, stood still, and looked around. This is a huge underground space, larger than the previous Hall of Bones, with the dome disappearing into darkness beyond sight.
The ground is some kind of gray-white slate, smooth and tidy, without any unnecessary debris. The air was quiet, no wind, no smell, and even the rotten smell that had been vaguely present before had disappeared.
There is nothing here.
Green's eyes scanned the entire space. null. Completely empty. It was as if someone had carefully removed every particle of dust here, leaving only this clean, empty space.
"Alice isn't here either."
Green said, his tone still seemed calm, but the annoyance inside was almost overflowing. His mind was getting increasingly unclear, and he wasn't sure what he would do if he didn't find Alice.
He was about to turn away, and then there was a roar.
From far to near, it looks like something is passing through the air at high speed. Green stopped and looked up.
The great white bird swooped down from the darkness of the dome. Its wings are four to five meters wide when spread out, and its feathers are an almost blinding white, which looks particularly clear in the dim light.
Its flight path was unlike that of a natural bird—straighter and more purposeful, like a shot arrow.
Green did not dodge. He stood there, raising his head, watching the big bird getting closer and closer until he could see its details clearly:
Its head is very long, much longer than a normal bird, and seems to be stretched. The face is covered with fine white feathers, but those feathers cannot hide the outline underneath - there is something not quite bird-like about the lines.
It has hair, golden hair. Hanging from the top of the head, like long human hair, it was blown backward by the wind during the high-speed dive. Those hair strands fluttered in the air with a faint, almost invisible luster.
"It's not Alice." Green said with great disappointment.
Even though the hair was blond, the blondness was different from Alice's. Alice's blond hair is bright and has the warmth of the sun. The big bird's blond hair was light and cold, as if it had been washed many times in the moonlight.
The big bird's mouth is open - it looks like a bird's beak and a human lip, with no clear boundary between the two. It let out a high-pitched whistle that vibrated the air.
Green moved, he stepped forward and punched the big bird in the head.
Big Bird's body was directly knocked off course. It rolled in the air for a circle and a half, and a few feathers fell down. Then it flapped its wings and stabilized again, landing some distance away.
It tilted its head and looked at Green. The eyes were amber, with vertical pupils—the eyes of a bird or something else.
Green looked at it, thinking about her possible relationship with Alice. Although she was not Alice, maybe she was related to Alice? If there is a connection, there may be clues about Alice.
The big bird didn't react much. It opened its mouth and uttered a vague syllable - as if it wanted to say something, but was blocked by something.
Then it took off again, this time without a head-on collision. It circled, flying around and around Green. As its wings flapped, the air was cut into invisible sharp blades.
Those wind blades hit Green from all directions, at extremely fast speeds and at tricky angles, turning and tracking in the air like living creatures.
